title: Bhikkhus, whatever in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among the multitude of ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, is seen ... examined…
content: Bhikkhus, whatever in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among the multitude of ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, is seen ... examined by the mind — all that I know. Bhikkhus, whatever in this world ... is seen ... examined by the mind — I have directly known it thus: 'All that the Tathāgata has known. The Tathāgata does not hold to it.' Bhikkhus, if I were to say: 'I know all that in this world ... is seen ... examined by the mind' — that would be false speech in me. If I were to say: 'I both know and do not know' — that would be false speech in me. If I were to say: 'I neither know nor do not know' — that would be false speech in me. Thus there would be an error in me.

title: Kassapa, one speaking rightly would say: 'One living the holy life must endure the hardships of the holy life. One living the holy life must…
content: Kassapa, one speaking rightly would say: 'One living the holy life must endure the hardships of the holy life. One living the holy life must be oppressed by the pressures of the holy life.' Speaking thus, Kassapa, one speaks rightly. One living the holy life must endure the hardships of the holy life. One living the holy life must be oppressed by the pressures of the holy life.

title: Bhikkhus, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, seeing beings with little dust in their eyes,…
content: Bhikkhus, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, seeing beings with little dust in their eyes, with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties, with dull faculties, with good qualities, with bad qualities, easy to teach, hard to teach, and some who saw the danger in future rebirth and the danger in faulty actions. Just as in a pond of blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses, some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, do not rise above the water, thrive while submerged; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, live reaching the water's surface; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, rise above the water and stand without being wetted by the water.

title: - Just as, bhikkhus, those families that have many women and few men are easily harassed by thieves and robbers. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu…
content: - Just as, bhikkhus, those families that have many women and few men are easily harassed by thieves and robbers. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who does not develop and cultivate the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is easily harassed by non-humans. - Just as, bhikkhus, those families that have few women and many men are not easily harassed by thieves and robbers. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is not easily harassed by non-humans. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will develop the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, cultivate it, make it our vehicle, make it our base, establish it, accumulate it, and properly undertake it.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

title: Elder Nun Soṇā: I gave birth to ten children From this accumulative body. Therefore I was weak and aged. I went to a bhikkhunī. She…
content:
Elder Nun Soṇā:

I gave birth to ten children
From this accumulative body.
Therefore I was weak and aged.
I went to a bhikkhunī.

She taught me the Dhamma,
About aggregates, sense spheres, and elements.
Hearing the Dhamma she taught,
I shaved my hair and went forth.

I followed her instruction.
My divine eye was purified,
I know my past lives,
Where I lived before.

I developed the signless Dhamma,
One-pointed, well concentrated.
Instantly I was liberated,
Without clinging, at peace.

The five aggregates are fully understood,
They stand with roots cut off.
I have no sensual desire,
No firm foundation.
From now on, there is no
Issue of renewed existence.

title: Elder Nun Sumānā: O that elder nun, Lie down happily, Covered in your robe, Made by yourself. Your greed is calmed, You are cooled, at…
content:
Elder Nun Sumānā:

O that elder nun,
Lie down happily,
Covered in your robe,
Made by yourself.
Your greed is calmed,
You are cooled, at peace.

title: When you gather together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done: discussing the Dhamma or maintaining noble silence." Then the Blessed One, having understood…
content:
When you gather together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done: discussing the Dhamma or maintaining noble silence." Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

One who lives without worldly work,
Light, desiring welfare,
With faculties restrained,
Fully liberated,

Homeless, without 'I-making',
Without sensual desire, having slain Māra,
Such a bhikkhu
Lives alone.

title: Elder Khitaka: My body is light, touched by great joy and bliss. Like cotton blown by the wind, my body floats.
content:
Elder Khitaka:

My body is light, touched by great joy and bliss.
Like cotton blown by the wind, my body floats.

title: There are these four inconceivable things, bhikkhus, that should not be speculated about; one who speculates about them would be subject to madness and distress.…
content: There are these four inconceivable things, bhikkhus, that should not be speculated about; one who speculates about them would be subject to madness and distress. What four? The sphere of a Buddha, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates about it would be subject to madness and distress. The sphere of one in meditation, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates... distress. The result of kamma, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates... distress. Speculation about the world, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates would be subject to madness and distress.

title: Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu dwells energetic and strenuous, abandoning unwholesome states, arousing wholesome states, steadfast, resolute, not discarding the burden regarding wholesome states. This is…
content: Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu dwells energetic and strenuous, abandoning unwholesome states, arousing wholesome states, steadfast, resolute, not discarding the burden regarding wholesome states. This is the fourth quality, Meghiya, that leads to the maturity of the unripe liberation of mind. Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu has wisdom, possessing wisdom that penetrates arising and passing away, with the noble penetration leading to the complete destruction of suffering. This is the fifth quality, Meghiya, that leads to the maturity of the unripe liberation of mind.
